title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool parallel calls, result injection, and retries
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: customer workloads and internal benchmarks showed brittle behavior when a single user request invoked multiple tools in parallel: inconsistent injection of tool outputs into the model context, opaques failures from transient tool errors surfaced to users, and streaming stability degraded when multiple tool streams were synthesized concurrently. This PR consolidates execution ergonomics for tool-calling to improve developer ergonomics and runtime robustness. Key changes: 1) Parallel tool executor: new executor that fans out tool invocations in parallel while preserving deterministic ordering policies for result injection (configurable per-route). 2) Result injection pipeline: unified model that normalizes tool outputs, applies output adapters (text/json/structured), and supports optional pinning of results into the conversation/KV cache with a clear TTL and provenance metadata. 3) Retry policies: first-class retry/backoff for transient tool failures with idempotency keys, per-tool retry limits, and circuit-breaker fallback to configured fallback-tools or graceful error responses. 4) Streaming stability: multiplexed stream merging with backpressure-aware buffer windows to avoid head-of-line blocking and to preserve partial-stream semantics for downstream SDKs. 5) OpenAI compatibility layer updates: small API surface adjustments to ensure that multi-tool responses and tool-call metadata (tool_name, status, diagnostics) are surfaced in the openai-compatible responses without changing existing top-level fields. Also added deprecation notes where necessary. Implementation details: changes are primarily in src/runtime/tool_executor.py (new ParallelToolExecutor, injection pipeline), src/api/handlers/tool_calling.py (route-level settings, compatibility layer), sdk/python/redwood/openai_compat.py (response adapters), sdk/typescript/src/tooling/stream_merger.ts (stream merging), and tests/e2e/tool-calling/* (behavioral and fault-injection tests). Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged (sequential invocation and legacy injection) unless a route enables parallel execution or the client opts into new injection semantics. This PR includes extensive unit/e2e tests and a migration guide. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4210) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] E2E failure-injection tests added - [x] SDK compatibility adapters added - [x] Updated docs and migration guide - [x] Benchmarked latency and cost impact (summary below) Benchmarks: parallel execution reduces median end-to-end latency for multi-tool flows by ~40% in high-latency tool networks, with a 5-12% increase in aggregate tool invocation cost depending on fan-out. Tradeoffs and mitigations are documented in the migration guide. Related: ENG-4302 implements a canary configuration for enabling parallel tool execution per-tenant.

review_comments: Ethan Park: Can we add an explicit idempotency key per tool invocation so retries don't double-apply side-effects? Author reply: Added idempotency keys and documented per-tool idempotency requirements in injection.md.

Lena Gomez: How does this interact with prefix/KV caching for prior tool outputs? Author reply: Injection pipeline now exposes a pin_to_kv option with TTL and provenance so cached items can be reused safely; added tests to verify TTL expiry behavior.

Omar Farooq: Concern about memory growth when many streams are merged. Author reply: StreamMerger uses bounded buffers and backpressure signals to the runtime; added circuit-breaker to reject large fan-outs and included a canary flag to roll out gradually.
ci_checks: benchmarks: perf-regression-check: pass (no regression beyond documented tradeoffs)
release_notes: Improved tool-calling ergonomics: support parallel multi-tool calls with deterministic result injection, configurable retry/backoff policies, and more stable streaming merging. Default behavior remains compatible. See docs/tool-calling/migration.md for details and route-level toggles.
tests_summary: unit: added 24 tests covering executor/retry/injection edge cases
e2e: added 6 end-to-end flows with faulty tool backends and streaming assertions
sdk: added compatibility tests in python and typescript SDKs
notes: Rollout plan: feature gated by route config; canary enabled for 10% traffic via ENG-4302. Observability: added per-tool metrics (invocations/retries/failures), stream merge latency histograms, and alerts for high retry rates. Follow-ups: add automatic tool affinity scheduling to co-locate low-latency tools on same node (future work).
